data.narrative:
Grain Weevil is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Chad and Ben Johnson that has raised $3.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public peer (277810.KQ), though a narrow peer set limits the applicability of traditional multiples-based approaches.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation framework, given data constraints. Using the $3.5M raised as a proxy base value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to the next funding stage yields an implied valuation of $9M. This reflects observed progression patterns across early-stage robotics companies transitioning out of seed, though the single-method reliance introduces concentration risk. A peer-median approach could not be executed: while ten robotics and manufacturing companies populate the broader sector comp set, fewer than three peers met narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables. Inclusion of all-sector medians would conflate companies across disparate development phases and valuations, introducing unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $7M to $10M, centered on $9M. The low-end estimate applies a modest discount to the stage-progression midpoint, while the high-end reflects upside optionality. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer validation, limited visibility into Grain Weevil's unit economics or technical differentiation, and reliance on a single methodological pillar. Subsequent rounds should prioritize collection of comparable seed and Series A transactions in the robotics subsector to narrow range width.
